simple.meaning: חֲיָא (chăyâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to live.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:4. The surrounding contexts include family line, death, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲיָא (H2418) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חֲיָא (chăyâʼ) / H2418 is traced through Daniel 2:4, Daniel 3:9, Daniel 5:10, Daniel 5:19 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.”

majorEvents.label: Death
majorEvents.evidenceText: Because of the greatness that he gave him, all the peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. He killed whom he wanted to, and he kept alive whom he wanted to. He raised up whom he wanted to, and he put down whom he wanted to.

timeline.evidenceText: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.”
They answered Nebuchadnezzar the king, “O king, live for ever!

The queen by reason of the words of the king and his lords came into the banquet house. The queen spoke and said, “O king, live forever; don’t let your thoughts trouble you, nor let your face be changed.

Because of the greatness that he gave him, all the peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. He killed whom he wanted to, and he kept alive whom he wanted to. He raised up whom he wanted to, and he put down whom he wanted to.

All the presidents of the kingdom, the deputies and the local governors, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a strong decree, that whoever asks a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me; because as before him innocence was found in me; and also before you, O king, I have done no harm.”
